subject.title: Bug: tools.deny does not hide skill_workshop from Codex deferred tools

question: Is current-main source-path proof enough to close this security-policy issue, or should it stay open until a live Codex app-server session verifies `tools.deny` propagation into deferred tools and developer instructions?
rationale: The shared source path now looks correct, but the issue describes an observed live session and the security-sensitive labels ask for maintainer/security review before a new fix lane.

options.title: Keep Open For Live Proof
options.body: Require a live or high-fidelity Codex app-server reproduction before closing or dispatching a code change.

options.title: Close As Source No-Repro
options.body: Treat the current source path and shipped release source check as sufficient evidence that the reported leak no longer matches current behavior.

options.title: Sponsor A Focused Regression PR
options.body: Use the closed candidate PR as test-shape input, but require maintainer ownership of any extra dynamic deny filter after deciding the policy boundary.

recommendation.title: Keep Open For Live Proof
recommendation.body: Require a live or high-fidelity Codex app-server reproduction before closing or dispatching a code change.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice spans the current Codex dynamic-tool path and shared tool-policy pipeline where recent ownership evidence points most strongly to steipete.
